text:
[LNAM.2.1.1] An identifier carries two independent properties. **Classification** —
whether it denotes a type reference or a binding — is by grammatical **position**
([LGRA]); case must not affect it. **Identity** — whether two identifiers
denote the same name — is **case-sensitive** and NFC-based ([LNAM.2.3]). Case
does not *classify*, and it does *distinguish*: `Reading` and `reading` are
two distinct identifiers, each legal in any position. The author may use case as
convention; the compiler must not require any case anywhere.
